one_line_contribution: Using one manufactured hidden rule change in ALFWorld and one partitioned expert pool on Qwen3-32B, measure and contrast two dose-response curves for the identical stale experience - harm as a function of how many of k=3 retrieved items are stale (claimed entry-gated and position-sensitive) versus harm as a function of the stale fraction p of a fixed-size QLoRA mix (claimed majority-gated under greedy decoding, linearizing under sampling) - and then test whether the two fitted curves quantitatively predict the recovery times of an unbounded bank and a continual LoRA on a single post-shift expert stream.
closest_prior_work: The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608, verified via s2cli, appears on both S2 and HF) is the nearest and the proposal is right that it is in-context only: it already establishes that a single conflicting retrieved trajectory is adopted at the first exposed decision point, compounds, and recovers weakly - which is most of P1's entry-gating content minus the fixed-token ladder and the position arm. Controlled Memory Interference (arXiv:2608.07622) I verified indirectly: `s2cli paper 2608.07622` returned 'not found on S2 or HF', but a title search returns it on S2 ('Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents', 2026-08-07, 1 citation), so the citation stands and the proposal's claim to have verified it is credible. The sharper threat the proposal never engages is on the weights side: 'Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-constant Number of Poison Samples' (arXiv:2510.07192, verified via s2cli search) reports that fine-tuning behaviour flips with a roughly fixed absolute count of conflicting examples independent of dataset fraction. At 30 % of the target partition (~2,700 examples), p=0.25 is already ~675 stale examples, far above that regime, so the null that P2 tries to reject - weights as brittle as context - is the prediction of published work, and the proposed ladder varies fraction and count together so it cannot separate them. On the context side, MemTrapBench (arXiv:2608.20202, found, uncited by the proposal) plus positional-bias work (arXiv:2507.22887; arXiv:2406.15981) and 'When Correct Demonstrations Hurt' (arXiv:2605.26350) already cover single-bad-item dominance and position sensitivity in prompts, so P1 mostly re-derives known ICL/RAG phenomena in a new environment. Also nearby but not colliding: 'How LoRA Remembers? A Parametric Memory Law for LLM Finetuning' (arXiv:2605.30260), a threshold-shaped law for LoRA memory.
strongest_objection: The pre-registered shape statistics are not resolvable at the pre-registered gate. Gate 0 only requires total stale harm >= 15 net points, and the proposal's own power section gives ~8 net points MDE for a difference between two dose levels. Distinguishing P1's f1 >= 0.6 from its falsifier f1 <= 0.4 is then a 3-net-point difference (0.2 x 15), and P2's quartile thresholds are worse: at 15 points of total harm, separating H(0.25)/H(1) <= 0.25 from a linear 0.4 is about 2 net points, and f1 and the quartile ratios are ratios of two noisy paired differences whose bootstrap CIs will span most of [0,1]. The sentence 'Gate 0 requires total stale harm >= 15 net points so that a 60 % vs 40 % split of the harm (P1) and the quartile thresholds (P2) are resolvable' is arithmetically wrong; the design needs roughly 40+ net points of harm, or many more seeds, before either law can be confirmed or falsified, and the plan states no branch for the most likely outcome (mid-range ratios, both P1 and P2 indeterminate). A second, independent objection: P6 is close to entailed by the arms chosen. An unbounded append-only bank retains all 300 pre-shift items forever while the continual LoRA's last 100-item chunk becomes 100 % fresh after the first post-shift update, so 'the bank recovers >= 2x slower' is largely a property of the two arms rather than of the fitted laws - exactly the definitional-headline failure for which the program archived opposite_sided_failure_under_shift, and the proposal adopts only two of the four fixes that rejection demanded (dose ladder and off-stream probe) while dropping the bounded evicting bank and the reset-LoRA arm.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-derive the gate from the shape statistics rather than the total: state the harm size H* at which f1's bootstrap CI excludes 0.5 and the quartile ratios exclude linearity given the seed budget, make that H* the Gate 0 threshold (strengthen the shift until it is met), and pre-register the 'ratios indeterminate' branch. (2) Make the two ladders comparable: run the in-context ladder at k=6 or 9 so d/k covers {0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1}, and add a count-matched parametric arm that holds the absolute number of stale examples fixed while varying the fresh count, so 'majority-gated' is separated from the near-constant-count result of 2510.07192, which should also be cited and treated as the competing hypothesis rather than ignored. (3) Restore the stream arms the program already demanded - bounded evicting bank, reset LoRA, and a replay LoRA - so the recovery-time contrast is a measurement rather than a consequence of append-only versus last-chunk-only, and pre-register the prediction band before those arms are run. (4) Drop or defer E5 and trim the E4 probe cadence to fit the stated two-to-three-day budget.
missing_baseline: The stream arms the binding Appendix-B objection required: a bounded evicting bank and a reset-LoRA arm (plus a self-generated-replay LoRA) alongside the unbounded bank and no-replay continual LoRA - without them P6's 2x recovery gap is a property of append-only versus last-chunk-only training, not of the fitted dose laws. Second omission: a stale-count-matched parametric cell (fixed absolute number of stale examples, varying fresh count) at more than one p, since the single p=0.5 data-size ablation cannot separate fraction from count.

Judging the check itself: it is above average for this program - three named queries, ids attached, honest that WebSearch was unavailable, and its citations survive verification - but it is scoped entirely to 'agent memory' phrasing and therefore misses both mechanism literatures its own predictions live in: the fine-tuning poison-dose thread (2510.07192) that directly disputes majority gating, and the ICL noisy-demonstration and positional-bias thread (2507.22887, 2406.15981, 2605.26350) plus MemTrapBench (2608.20202) that already supplies much of entry gating. A collision check that does not search the literature of the effect it predicts understates the threat, and here it does.
